Flow (high level): Frontend form submits the GitHub URL to POST /api/index on the backend. (client UI: RepoConnector.jsx) server/src/app.js (POST /api/index) calls addIndexingJob(...) from server/src/jobs/queue.js. app.js immediately returns HTTP 202 with jobId. server/src/jobs/queue.js uses BullMQ to add the job into the Redis-backed queue (QUEUE_NAME = 'indexing-queue', job name 'index-repo'). A separate background process running server/src/jobs/indexingWorker.js (a BullMQ Worker) picks up jobs from 'indexing-queue' and invokes indexRepository(...) in server/src/services/indexingPipeline.js to run the heavy pipeline (clone → walk → chunk → embed → save). The worker updates job progress and returns a result.

Minimal / must-update locations: server/src/services/embeddingService.js — the code and comments assume the model and dimensionality (EMBEDDING_MODEL = 'openai/text-embedding-3-small'; comments reference 1536). If you change to a different model that returns 1024-d vectors, update the EMBEDDING_MODEL constant and any logic/comments expecting 1536. server/supabase/match_chunks.sql — the SQL function signature currently declares query_embedding vector(1536). Update vector(1536) → vector(1024) and any SQL that assumes 1536-length vectors.

Trigger (backend): server/src/app.js (POST /api/chat) streams LLM content via SSE in standard (non-strict) mode; it accumulates the response text into accumulatedResponse. After streaming completes it calls validateCitations(accumulatedResponse, chunks). If hallucinations are found, app.js writes an SSE event: data: JSON.stringify({ type: 'hallucination_warning', invalidFiles: hallucinations }) File: server/src/app.js — SSE streaming loop + post-stream validateCitations + res.write of hallucination_warning. Frontend reaction: client/src/components/ChatWindow.jsx reads the response body (response.body.getReader()), decodes chunks, splits into lines, and for lines starting with 'data: ' it JSON.parse()s the data. If parsed.type === 'hallucination_warning', it updates the last AI message object with a hallucinationWarning field (setMessages(...)).

What happens when parser fails: server/src/services/chunker/astChunker.js calls parser.parse(content) inside a try/catch. If parse throws, the catch logs a warning and returns chunkFileNaive(content, filePath, options). (astChunker.js try/catch and fallback return) chunkFileNaive (server/src/services/chunker/naiveChunker.js) produces line-based chunks (chunkSize default 50, overlap 10). chunker/index.js routes files to astChunker or naiveChunker by extension. The indexing pipeline (server/src/services/indexingPipeline.js) accumulates allChunks (including naive chunks returned from the AST chunker fallback), filters out empty/whitespace-only chunks: const validChunks = allChunks.filter(chunk => chunk.content && chunk.content.trim().length > 0); embedChunks(validChunks) is invoked to generate embeddings for each valid chunk.

RRF in SQL: server/supabase/match_chunks.sql implements the hybrid retrieval and RRF score. The RRF-like formula used in that SQL is: (COALESCE(1.0 / (60 + vector_search.vector_rank), 0.0) + COALESCE(1.0 / (60 + keyword_search.keyword_rank), 0.0))::float as rrf_score. How backend calls it: server/src/services/retrievalService.js computes a query embedding (generateEmbedding(question)) and then calls the Postgres RPC via Supabase: await supabase.rpc('match_chunks', { query_embedding: queryEmbedding, query_text: question, match_count: matchCount, repo_id: repositoryId });

Lifecycle of status: When indexing begins, indexRepository inserts a row in repositories with status: 'indexing'. (server/src/services/indexingPipeline.js — .insert({... status: 'indexing' ...})). On successful completion the pipeline updates that repository row to status: 'completed' and sets total_files, total_chunks, updated_at. (indexingPipeline.js). If an error is thrown during the pipeline, the catch block updates the repository row to status: 'failed' and writes error_message + updated_at, then performs cleanup. (indexingPipeline.js).

Initialization: server/src/config/redis.js creates and returns a REDIS configuration object (REDIS_CONFIG / REDIS_CONF) suitable for BullMQ (it constructs host/port/defaults; module exports createRedisConnection function / config). Sharing: Both server/src/jobs/queue.js (the producer/Queue) and server/src/jobs/indexingWorker.js (the consumer/Worker) import server/src/config/redis.js (or the exported REDIS_CONFIG) and pass it as the connection option when instantiating new Queue(...) or new Worker(...). That ensures both use the same Redis target.

Backend setup: server/src/app.js uses helmet for security headers: app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: false, crossOriginEmbedderPolicy: false })); and it enables CORS with app.use(cors()); it also sets express.json() for request parsing. These middlewares run for all incoming requests before route handlers. Frontend requests: Frontend components use fetch() to the API host (e.g., ChatWindow.jsx uses fetch('http://localhost:3001/api/chat', ...) and RepoConnector.jsx polls GET /api/index/status/:jobId). Because CORS is enabled on the backend, those cross-origin requests from the React app are accepted.

Where and how: server/src/services/embeddingService.js implements generateEmbeddingsBatch(texts) that wraps the openai.embeddings.create(...) call inside a retry loop. It sets MAX_RETRIES = 3 and, on retryable errors (error.status === 429 or server errors 5xx or unexpected responses), waits with exponential backoff (comments and code indicate delays doubling: 2000ms → 4000ms → 8000ms) before retrying. If final attempt fails it throws the error upward.

Where: Validation logic lives in server/src/services/citationValidator.js — extractFilePaths(text) uses a regex to extract path-like tokens; validateCitations(generatedText, retrievedChunks) compares those extracted paths to the set of file_path values returned by the retrieval RPC (the chunks passed in). Why it’s separate: The LLM answer is streamed in standard mode (server/src/app.js uses generateAnswerStream and writes SSE deltas as they arrive). Because the textual output is streamed incrementally, the server only has access to the complete generated text after the stream finishes.
